sentences.text:
Shri Sankalp Kochar - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Ajay Tamrakar - Panel Lawyer for the State.
 Shri Aditya Khare - Advocate for the objector.

Order 
This is second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR/Crime No. 392/2024 dated 29.5.2024 registered at Police Station Govindpura, District Bhopal for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 294, 506 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Earlier application of the applicant for anticipatory bail filed vide M.Cr.C. No. 25287 of 2024 was dismissed was dismissed on merit vide order dated 2.7.2024.
3. The counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.

It is submitted that the previous application of the applicant for anticipatory bail was dismissed on the basis of whatsapp chat between the applicant and the prosecutrix and also the application given by the applicant to the Town Inspector, where the applicant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40631 2 MCRC-30504-2024 assured the complainant to enter into wedlock.

It is submitted by the counsel that the whatsapp chat, on the basis of which previous application was dismissed, di not occur between the applicant and the prosecutrix and the applicant never assured the prosecutrix of marriage in February.

It is further submitted that no certificate Gourav Vijayvargiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92942367/
1 under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act was produced by the complainant to authenticate the said whatsapp chat, therefore, they cannot be said to be trustworthy.

In support of the aforesaid contentions, the counsel of the applicant has placed reliance on the decision of the Apex Court in Criminal Appeal No. 1552 of 2023 (Shiv Pratap Singh Rana Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh and another) - 2024 INSC 481 decided on 8.7.2024 and the order passed by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.
10765 of 2023 (Abhishek Deshbhartar Vs. The State of M.P.) and another - decided on 15.5.2024.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the applicant is ready to cooperate in the investigation and trial.

Therefore,
the applicant is enlarged on anticipatory bail.

4. The counsels for the State as well as objector have opposed the application and submit that earlier application of the applicant for anticipatory bail has already been dismissed by this Court by passing an elaborate order.

No new ground has been taken by the applicant in this repeat application,
therefore, this application is liable to be dismissed.

5. Heard the submissions and perused the case diary.
6.

This repeat application has been filed on behalf of the applicant seeking anticipatory bail on the ground that the whatsapp chat filed by the prosecution did not occur and it was manipulated and no certificate under NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:40631 3 MCRC-30504-2024 Section 65-B of the Indian Evidence Act was filed in support of the said whatsapp chat.

Earlier application of the applicant was dismissed by this court while observing that there are direct allegations by the complainant that under the garb of false promise of marriage, the present applicant compelled the complainant to have intercourse twice without her consent.
The Court also observed that the FIR also reflects that complainant was given medicinal tablets by the applicant for abortion as the complainant had conceived.

It was also observed by this Court that the whats-app chats of the applicant as well as complainant also prima facie suggests that applicant herein had assured the complainant to enter into wedlock with her.
7. This Court while passing the order dated 2.7.2024 in M.Cr.C. No. 25287 of 2024 has already considered all the aspects of the case on merit by a detailed order.

The veracity of the whatsapp chat,
is a subject matter of evidence and it cannot be gone into in an application seeking anticipatory bail.
Therefore, looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is not inclined to enlarge the applicant on anticipatory bail.
8. Accordingly, the application stands dismissed.

(MANINDER S. BHATTI) JUDGE PB Gourav Vijayvargiya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92942367/
